title: Font stacks and weights
summary: A font-family stack with fallbacks, and the weights from 400 to 800 that build hierarchy.
explanation: font-family takes a list. The browser uses the first font it has, so the list ends with a generic family (sans-serif, serif, monospace) that always exists. system-ui means the operating system's own interface font, which looks native and needs no download.
font-weight runs from 100 (thin) to 900 (black); 400 is normal and 700 is bold. Most system fonts have several weights in between, so 500 and 600 give softer emphasis than jumping straight to bold.
If a font lacks a weight, the browser picks the nearest one or fakes bold by smearing the letters, which is why weights sometimes look the same.
tryThis: Change .serif's font-family to Georgia, serif and then to a made-up name followed by serif: the fallback takes over.
Set every .weight to font-weight: 700: the hierarchy flattens.
Change .mono's stack to just monospace and compare the digits.
